ADVISORY (non-blocking, not a fidelity defect): the German gloss delimiters {%...%} are dropped in every Russian rendering (1a, 1b, 1c, 2, PW1a, PW1b, PW1c). The stripping is uniform across all senses, so it reads as an intentional pipeline convention (the {%...%} span is exactly what gets translated), but if downstream consumers expect the italic/gloss markers to survive into the RU column, they are absent.

Senses tag 1, 2a (first block) and tag 1, 2a (second block): German has TWO distinct glosses — 'zum Laufen bringend' (causative of dru: 'заставляющий бежать / приводящий в движение') and 'in die Flucht jagend/schlagend' ('обращающий в бегство'). The Russian renders both as put-to-flight synonyms ('приводящий в бегство, обращающий в бегство'), dropping the first meaning and producing a tautological pair. Same in the nominal forms: 'das zum-Laufen-Bringen, in-die-Flucht-Jagen' -> 'приведение в бегство, обращение в бегство'; expected 'побуждение к бегу / приведение в движение, обращение в бегство'.

Sense {T87} (1. anarta 2〉): German {%sich auf Unheil verstehend%} ('versed in / knowing how to work mischief') is rendered «sведущий в беде», which reads as 'knowledgeable about misfortune' rather than 'skilled at causing harm'; the parallel gloss immediately after ({%Unheil zu stiften verstehend%} → «умеющий причинять беду») shows the intended active nuance. Sense 9 / PW 14.2: German "um sein Ansehen gekommen" (paired with "verwelkt") is rendered "потерявший свое достоинство". In this entry Ansehen elsewhere is consistently taken as physical appearance (PW 7bβ "ein leidendes, verstelltes Ansehen habend" → "имеющий страдальческий, искаженный вид"; sense 1 "ein welkes ... Ansehen erhält" → "получает вялый ... вид"). The pun on withering favours "утративший свой (прежний) вид" / "потерявший привлекательный вид"; "достоинство" narrows it to social standing and breaks internal consistency. Minor, not a hard defect.

Sense 2 gloss {%reisig%} rendered as {%верхом%} (adverb, 'on horseback'). The German is an adjective meaning 'конный, верховой' (of a mounted warrior); an adverbial rendering breaks the adjectival gloss series of this entry. Substitute {%конный%}.

Sense "PW 1", subsense 2〉b〉: German meta-label "{%vor%} (zeitlich)" is rendered "{%перед%} (временно)". Russian «временно» means "temporarily", not "temporally / in the temporal sense" — it misstates the grammatical note (its sibling 2〉a〉 "(räumlich)" → «пространственно» is correct). Fix to «(во временном значении)» or «(о времени)»; for parity 2〉a〉 may read «(о месте)» / «(в пространственном значении)».

Sense "PW 1", subsense 1〉e〉: German "(als die Krieger)" is rendered "(чем кшатрии)". "Krieger" = warriors; substituting the varṇa term «кшатрии» imports a specific technical identification not present in Böhtlingk's German. Use «(чем воины)» to stay faithful.

Sense 1: "Einfluss auf den Ton des verbi finiti" is rendered as "влияние на тон глагола" — the Latin technical specification *verbi finiti* (the FINITE verb) is dropped, widening the claim from the finite verb to any verb. Restore the scope, e.g. "влияние на ударение (тон) verbi finiti" / "...личной формы глагола". Note also that in PWG's accentual terminology 'Ton' is the word-accent (ударение), so "тон" alone risks a phonetic-pitch misreading.

Sense 1: "(so {T134} {T135} zu lesen {T136})" → "(так {T134} {T135} читать {T136})" — the German 'zu lesen' is deontic ('is to be read / should be read'); the bare Russian infinitive loses that modality. Use "(так следует читать {T134} {T135} ... {T136})" or "...надлежит читать...".

Sense 1, structural note mistranslated: German "am {T114} eines {T115} in dieser {T116}:" is rendered "у {T114} одного {T115} в этом {T116}:". Two errors: (a) "am" (= "am Anfang/Ende", a position-in-compound note) becomes "у" ("at/with"), losing the positional sense; (b) the genitive article "eines" is read as the numeral "one" and rendered "одного", inventing a quantity not in the German. The parallel construction later in the same sense — "Am Ende eines {T184}" → "В конце {T184}" — shows the correct handling (positional preposition + no article), so this earlier instance is inconsistent with the translation's own practice. Fix to e.g. "в {T114} {T115} в этом {T116}:" (mirroring "В конце {T184}").

Sense tag "3" (first block) and tag "4" (root-summary block): German {%betreiben, urgere%} is rendered {%побуждать, понуждать%}, which (a) silently DROPS the Latin equivalent "urgere" — PWG's Latin glosses are part of the entry's scholarly content and are normally retained verbatim — and (b) makes this sense verbally identical to the first half of {%anregen, drängen; fördern, begeistern%} (also {%побуждать, понуждать%}), collapsing two distinct PWG senses into indistinguishable Russian. Sense tag "1a" (first block), Böhtlingk's conjectural rendering: German {%den%} {T120} {%decket%} — "den" is the accusative definite article governing the masked object, but the Russian has {%его%} ("his/its"), inventing a possessive absent from the German; it should be article-less or a demonstrative ({%тот%}). In the same clause {%mit%} is rendered {%чем%} ("with what/than"), which reads as interrogative rather than the instrumental preposition — German "mit + noun" should surface as bare instrumental of {T122} or {%с%}.
